_comment: UAE jurisdiction profile — CBUAE product governance (Consumer Protection Standards: comprehensive product approval, inherent-risk assessment, documented control-function sign-off; Operational Risk Art. 11: new/materially changed products and systems). Pure data, composed over regulated-bank; authored with the open-finance-uae skill as reference, never a runtime dependency.
_automatic_profiles_comment: 2.4.0 — a UAE new or materially changed product that declares a model in its decision path automatically compiles the ai-decision-system profile. This closes the profile-omission gap: the classifier supplies facts, and jurisdiction policy derives the route. It is intentionally narrower than every use of a model — internal engineering assistants remain under the regulated-bank model-risk conditional unless they are part of a product change. The rule implements the CBUAE February 2026 consumer-AI guidance scope (AI/ML use bearing on consumers); an institution may add broader automatic rules, never delete this one while claiming this shipped profile unchanged.

conditional._comment: Open Finance in this market carries a MANDATED customer-experience regime — the AlTareq brand and CX rules for consent screens, payment buttons and progress indication, with screen certification. It is attached to the JURISDICTION and not to products/open-finance deliberately: every market with an Open Finance regime has a CX regime, and they are different regimes. Putting this in the product profile would export one market's brand rules to all of them; putting it here means another market's jurisdiction profile carries its own, and the product profile stays market-neutral.

2.1.0 (hardening plan 4.2 · 4.4). The personal_data conditional that compiled a prose `pdpl-and-residency` section is RETIRED: the base profile now compiles the `dpia` capability on that flag, and the DPIA record carries residency as a field the gate reads. The third_party conditional binds the CBUAE Outsourcing Regulation's assessment at PA1 — a materiality assessment, the notification or non-objection position, and the exit plan — for every outsourcing the change introduces or relies on. An LLM provider is one of these (the model manifest's third_party block is where the per-provider assessment lives, and scripts/product-approval-check.mjs requires it); so is an evidence platform such as Kosli.
